about: Typed relations the text states but ingest doesn't derive (GR-15, GR-06): an exception modifies a rule, a preemption can override it, a provision uses a definition. Each quotes the words in its 'from' provision that state the relation. A provisional reading by CC (2026-11-01), for the Portland detached-ADU slice; other relations are not modeled yet and an agent must read the text.

relations.quote: may extend into a required building setback up to 20 percent of the depth of the setback
Building eaves may extend up to 2 feet into a required building setback
may extend into the entire required building setbacks
The front building setback, and the setback of decks, balconies, and porches may be reduced to the average of the respective setbacks on the abutting lots
the front building setback for the dwelling may be reduced to 10 feet
The height limit in the area of the reduced setback is lowered one foot for every foot of reduced setback
relations.note: An exception to an exception: it limits the reduced front setback (recursive family membership).

relations.quote: are allowed in required side and rear building setbacks if all of the following are met
relations.note: For detached covered accessory structures, ADUs among them (33.110.245.C; 33.205.040.C.3).

relations.quote: a local government may adopt and apply only clear and objective standards, conditions and procedures regulating: (A) The development of housing
relations.note: Overrides a housing standard only where it is not clear and objective; Portland's setbacks are numeric. ORLAW 2025 c.330 s.8(2) excludes setbacks from its design-standard limit, so it is not recorded as a preemption here.

relations.quote: from a side street lot line
The structure is no more than 15 feet high
Setbacks are usually measured from lot lines
A lot, adjusted lot, lot remnant, or lot of record
the development standards for covered accessory structures in the base zone
relations.note: The ADU's route into 33.110.245's accessory-structure standards.
